title: Simple characteristic quotients of torsion-free non-elementary hyperbolic groups embedding any countable group with prescribed torsion and outer automorphisms
author: Rémi Coulon; Francesco Fournier-Facio
difficulty_reason: The cited small-cancellation theorem yields one controlled quotient, but does not itself produce a characteristic simple limit with a prescribed embedded countable group and faithful outer action. The authors build the new normal-closure iteration while preserving a protected injectivity ball and the exact quotient by the ambient normal subgroup, then use elliptic-subgroup control to preserve every finite element order at the limit. A separate free-product embedding stage and the fully written finite-relation centralizer argument retain the countable subgroup and force the outer-automorphism map to be injective.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem4.1: torsion-free non-elementary hyperbolic group Gamma, finite subset C and arbitrary countable group L. A characteristic quotient is simple, 2-generated, not finitely presentable, injective on C, contains L, has exactly the finite element orders of L, and admits an embedding Out(Gamma) into its outer automorphism group. Full countable-group embedding core14–15 and closing characteristic construction15–16 read; full new iterative small-cancellation simplicity/torsion/outer-action core10–12 read. Definitions and suitable subgroup arguments5–9 retained. Named Hull2016 Theorem7.1 small-cancellation, Osin acylindricity, classical countable-group embedding preserving torsion LS01 IV.3.1, and published acylindrical hyperbolicity of automorphism groups are traced prerequisites. No arbitrary acylindrically hyperbolic Gamma assertion or finitely-presented final quotient. Quasi-isometric diversity Section5 and continuum-count consequence are not separately counted.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors combine acylindrical small cancellation with an automorphism-group construction, embed a countable group elliptically, and iterate normal-generation quotients while retaining finite injectivity, torsion and outer-automorphism control. This infinite group construction exceeds ordinary qualifying examinations.
